WHY ONLY THREE IDEAS, AND WHY THAT IS THE FLOORS WORKING. The tape offered one real opportunity set — the rotation out of AI into value and defensives — and it had already happened. DG sits 4.12% off its high and KR 2.37% off theirs, so an honest 2+ ATR stop on either forces a target roughly 10% ABOVE the prior range high. That is the reward-to-risk floor rejecting ideas from the TARGET side rather than the stop side, and stretching a target to clear it is the same sin as walking a stop in. Six ideas were rejected on arithmetic alone (DG, KR, MU, a crypto short, an HYG short, the Dec 1-3 software shorts), three on evidence (CSCO, SCHW, ORCL), four on having no defensible edge (both CPI YoY months, the Fed decision, November unemployment), one on the correlation cap before any merit test (UNH), one on internal coherence (a gold short, whose main risk is this report's own highest-conviction macro view), and one on the DG/KR test again (EXEL, the nearest FDA catalyst). Padding the list would have meant publishing names the research had just finished disqualifying.

THE CLUSTERING IS REAL AND YOU SHOULD KNOW ABOUT IT. All three ideas are swing stock longs, all three score conviction 4, and all three recompute to a reward-to-risk of EXACTLY 2.00 against a 2.0 swing floor. Three ratios landing on the floor is precisely the signature CLAUDE.md warns about — targets fitted to clear the bar — so here is the check, recomputed in synthesis from the entry, target and stop rather than trusted from the notes, with ATR re-fetched from source: DKS risk 15.50 / reward 31.00, stop 2.06 ATR (ATR14 7.5267); LULU risk 10.55 / reward 21.10, stop 2.23 ATR (ATR14 4.7213); GIII risk 2.69 / reward 5.38, stop 2.59 ATR (ATR14 1.0406). Every stop clears the 2.0 ATR stock swing floor on the WIDE side, so the ratio was not bought with a tight stop, and each target is an identifiable level rather than a number reverse-engineered from the floor: DKS 175.50 is 14.8x the newly raised FY26 non-GAAP EPS midpoint of $11.88 (below a market multiple), LULU 127.15 is the 127.31 SMA200, GIII 37.07 is a retest of the 37.54 range high from below. Win probabilities (45%, 43%, 42%) all sit above the 33.3% break-even baseline implied by 1/(1+2), claiming 9-12 points of edge — modest and deliberately so. But the honest caveat stands: ratios at the floor mean these three have no margin for error in the levels, and the report would rather say that than round the numbers up.

THE MOST IMPORTANT CONTENT TODAY IS NOT A CANDIDATE, IT IS THE REGIME AND ONE OPEN POSITION. LANES REACHED AND DECLINED, not skipped: event contracts (Fed decision, both CPI YoY months, unemployment — all efficiently priced), crypto, shorts across software and the gold complex, financials, small and micro caps, and FDA/PDUFA dates. Four small caps were struck on hard universe floors rather than judgement: CRMT trades under $1 with a 71.48% ATR, SPWH has $0.3M average dollar volume and TLYS $0.5M (at or below the $500K floor), and NNE's 12.10% ATR makes a 2.0 ATR stop 24% wide. TWO MECHANICAL VALIDATION FLAGS THE RED TEAM SHOULD READ BEFORE ACTING ON THEM. First, the bid/ask spreads attached to these three ideas are a PRE-MARKET DATA ARTIFACT, not a real book, and they should not be read as a liquidity finding. The depth endpoint returned DKS 150.00/158.88 (a 5.75% 'spread' that simply brackets the 148.75-157.89 session range), GIII 13.78/50.70 (a 114.5% 'spread' against a 31.69 last — that is not a two-sided quote by any reading), and LULU 103.00/105.59 (below the 104.00-108.57 range). US equities are closed at this hour, so there is no regular-hours book to sample. The honest liquidity evidence is the measured average dollar volume carried on each idea: DKS $352M and LULU $339M are deeply liquid, and GIII at $12.3M on 387,478 shares a day genuinely IS a thin small cap — which is why it is sized at 2% and why its entry condition requires limit orders rather than market orders. Second, DKS's `catalyst.datetime_et` is deliberately NULL rather than backdated to 2026-11-24. The validator is right that a catalyst in the past is not a catalyst; the truthful statement for a held position is that the event already fired and confirmed the thesis, so there is nothing left to position around. Dressing the 2026-12-11 dividend record date up as the catalyst to satisfy a date field would be padding, and no Q4 earnings date is asserted because none was fetched — DKS does not appear on the 14-day calendar this run pulled. All three ideas also carry a '2 of 2 sources could not be verified' warning, which in this case means what the warning itself says it might: every source on this page is an sec.gov EDGAR URL, and sec.gov refuses automated fetches from the validator's user agent. Each was read during research — the DKS 8-K Exhibit 99.1 and dividend 8-K, the LULU 8-K seating Tara Poseley and Wilson's 13D/A Amendment 25, and the GIII Form 4 and 8-K indexes — and the figures quoted come from those documents, not from stories about them.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). CUT TWO OF THREE, ONE SURVIVES. DKS was cut from rank 1 and carried to the watchlist as an unchanged HOLD instruction: it was filled 2026-11-16, its target and stop are identical to the stored row, and its entry condition says 'Nothing to do at the open', so the published 2.0:1 is a ratio from a fill that already happened — the ratio available at the 153.17 close is 0.92:1, below the floor every other idea had to clear. The report reached the opposite conclusion about itself twice on the same page (the IWM short withheld because 'holding an existing short is not a new idea', OXY routed to the watchlist for want of an exit primitive), and publish_sheets.apply_amendment records nothing at all for a republication at unchanged levels. The hold is right; ranking it first was not. It also asked for 3% against a stored 2% while telling the reader to do nothing. GIII was KILLED: the thesis claims an edge in 'a name the market has not re-rated' while citing +12.97pp of one-month relative strength and a close above all three moving averages, which is the same fact read two ways; its pillar is a ten-week-old insider buy at $27.94 that the 31.69 entry is already +13.4% above; and its 2.0:1 and +0.29R are both computed from a 29.00 stop fill that its own key_risk says a $12.3M-ADV small cap gaps through on a binary 12-02 print at a company with a -49.94% miss in its record. LULU survives at rank 1, conviction 4 CHECKED AND KEPT (three real independent confirmations), with four fixes: win probability 42% to 38% (+0.14R, 4.7 points of claimed edge) because the only path to a +20% target inside a 15-session horizon is a ~4.5 ATR gap on the print; the entry zone narrowed 104.00-108.50 to 105.00-106.05; key_risk rewritten; and the counter-argument reframed around the shape of the trade rather than the story.

FOUR FINDINGS THE MECHANICAL CHECKS CANNOT SEE, RECORDED FOR THE REPO RATHER THAN FOR TODAY. (1) EVERY PUBLISHED ENTRY ZONE BROKE A FLOOR AT BOTH ENDS, on all three ideas, because check_risk_reward and check_stop_distance read `entry.ideal` and never `zone_low`/`zone_high`. LULU 104.00-108.50 ran from a 1.80 ATR stop at the bottom to 1.43:1 at the top; GIII 30.60-32.20 from a 1.54 ATR stop to 1.52:1; DKS 142.00-147.00 to 1.58:1 at the top. In each case only the ideal price passed, and it passed exactly. A zone is what a reader actually fills in, so the floors should be enforced across it — GIII's honest band was 31.08-31.69, 0.59 ATR wide, which is the fact that made it unexecutable rather than merely thin. (2) ALL THREE TARGETS COMPUTED TO EXACTLY 2.0000x RISK TO THE PENNY (15.50/31.00, 2.69/5.38, 10.55/21.10). Checked rather than assumed, and the defence holds: each nearby real level — SMA200 127.31, range high 37.5387, 14.8x at 175.82 — clears 2.0 on its own (2.015, 2.17, 2.02), so each target was rounded DOWN to the floor rather than stretched up to it. The exactness is still a tell that the floor, not the chart, set the last decimal. (3) THE CLAIMED WIN PROBABILITIES ARE CONTRADICTED BY THIS REPORT'S OWN RECORD AND NOTHING ADDRESSED IT. The three ideas claimed 45/43/42% against a 33.3% break-even; closed stock trades here are 2/33 on target (6%) at -7.5% average and swings 5/42 (12%), both below break-even, on an n that prior_context's own 15-trade threshold says is not noise. The partial defence is real — CLAUDE.md records that all ten of the first month's stop-outs had stops tighter than 1.6 ATR and today's clear 2.0 — but it does not cover LULU's own prior long (17.8% stop, stopped anyway) or ONON's (10.3% stop, stopped 2026-11-20). A 42% claim in a 6-12% category needs the mechanism named; only LULU's was, and it was cut to 38% for it. (4) THE SECTOR BASE RATE WAS NEVER CONSULTED. Discretionary retail and apparel longs are 0 for 7 here (NKE, TJX, HD, DG, LULU, ONON, plus DKS still open and -7.5% below entry at last mark), and the shorts stopped out too (LULU, NKE), so the pattern is mistiming this sector rather than a direction. ONON — premium athleisure, long, conviction 4, stopped 2026-11-20, three sessions ago — is the nearest comparable to today's surviving idea and appeared nowhere in the report. It is now in LULU's key_risk.

ON THE CORRELATION TEST AND THE SPREAD FAILURES. The report disclosed its own clustering honestly and was right that three ideas in one sector sits AT strategy.md's cap of three rather than over it, so the cluster was not itself a reason to cut; it resolved as a by-product of killing GIII and de-listing DKS, leaving one discretionary long against DKS held. Separately, synthesis was right about the two mechanical `fail` verdicts and the red team is not overriding them on faith: GIII's 13.78/50.70 book against a 31.69 last and DKS's 150.00/158.88 bracketing the prior session's 148.75-157.89 range are closed-market artifacts, not liquidity findings — US equities have no regular-hours book at 06:43 ET and check_spread has no session guard, unlike check_price_freshness. Both were cut on their merits instead, and the watchlist records those merits rather than the artifact, so phase 2d has nothing left to demote on a reason that is not true.

market_context.summary: The regime is TIGHTENING, and that is the most important fact in this report. Kalshi prices the 2026-12-09 FOMC at 92-93 cents for a 25bp HIKE and ~95-96% cumulative for a hike of some size, on 5.5M open interest — deep, liquid pricing, not a thin market. October FOMC minutes have nearly all 19 officials expecting a December increase, Waller has floated a half-point, and St. Louis's Musalem says the economy will likely need several increases before spring 2027. This is a cycle, not one hike. It is arriving into a disinflationary commodity bust and an AI correction: USO -21.2% off its high, GLD -24.2%, QQQ -16.4%, SPY -8.0% and both indices below their 20- and 50-day averages, with BTC at $58.8K (-21% from where a 2026-11-09 short entry sat unfilled). That is a policy-error setup, and the long end is already trading it — TLT rallied from 79.55 to 81.49 while December hike odds went to 92, a bull flattener rather than the duration headwind a hiking Fed would normally imply. 2026-11-24 itself was a violent factor rotation, not a selloff: SMH -7.26% and XLK -3.26% against M +6.30%, KR +4.42%, DG +3.33% and XLP +1.66%, with the Dow CLOSING UP 423 points at 50,019 while SPY fell 0.49%. The cleanest read on the driver is not NVDA (whose +31.5% then -5.86% was Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO, governance rather than fundamentals) but HPE: it BEAT and still fell 16.31% on Cloud & AI margin guidance. The market has stopped paying for AI revenue and started pricing AI returns — into a Fed that is raising the discount rate on exactly those debt-financed buildouts. October PCE lands at 08:30 ET TODAY (verified on the BEA release schedule) alongside the Q3 GDP second estimate, and it is the last inflation print before that FOMC; the next is 2026-12-23, after the meeting. The asymmetry matters: with a December hike already 92% priced, a soft print can only soften the 2027 path, while a hot print can sharply reprice a >25bp tail that Kalshi has at just 3-4 cents. So do not front-run it. Markets are then CLOSED Thursday 2026-11-26 for Thanksgiving and trade a half session to 1pm ET on Friday 2026-11-27. The honest conclusion of the morning's work is that the defensive/value rotation this regime calls for has ALREADY happened: DG sits 4.12% and KR 2.37% off their own highs. Buying the receiving end of the rotation today means buying within a few percent of all-time highs, where an honest 2+ ATR stop forces a target above the prior range high. The names are right and the entries are gone.

recommendations.thesis: Not a bet on the consumer — a bet on a founder-forced product reset in a name where expectations have already capitulated. Chip Wilson holds 8.6% (9,570,851 shares, 13D/A Amendment 25) and under a 2026-05-26 cooperation agreement the board was expanded from twelve to thirteen on 2026-10-19 to seat Tara Poseley, who was lululemon's own Chief Product Officer from 2013-2015 — the appointment targets precisely the product and brand-momentum failure that took the stock 44.9% off its high. Sell-side positioning is washed out at 4.8% bullish (1 strong buy, 1 buy, 31 hold, 6 sell, 3 strong sell), yet the company beat consensus in three of its last four quarters, including by 12.5% last quarter.
recommendations.key_risk: Earnings gap risk is the live danger and 2026-12-09 doubles it: the FOMC decides at 14:00 ET that day and lululemon reports at 16:05 ET, so the 2026-12-10 open prices a 92%-priced hike (with a 3-4 cent >25bp tail that is where the repricing risk actually sits) and the quarter at once. ATR14 is 4.45%, so that open can gap straight through the 95.50 stop rather than filling it — which is why this is 2%, and why a realised loss can exceed 1R and the +0.14R expectancy with it. THE STOP SITS IN A ZONE THAT HAS ALREADY BEEN REACHED: 95.50 is below the 101.55 and 102.20 swing lows and below the 101.78 SMA50, but it is only 5.7% above the 90.38 52-week low in a name trading 16.7% under a declining SMA200, so an ordinary retest of the cycle low takes it out — and this report's own prior LULU long was stopped at 94.50, one dollar below it. THE BASE RATE IS AGAINST THIS TRADE AND IS NOT NOISE: consumer-discretionary retail and apparel longs published by this report are 0 for 7 — NKE -13.2%, TJX -4.0%, HD -3.5%, DG -6.8% (conviction 4), LULU itself -17.8% (conviction 3), ONON -10.3% (conviction 4) — and the sector has stopped out shorts too (LULU -11.3%, NKE -6.8%), so the losses are not directional, they are this report mistiming this sector. ONON is the one to weigh: premium athleisure, long, conviction 4, opened 2026-11-03 and stopped 2026-11-20, three sessions before this report. LULU specifically is 0 for 2. Beyond that: this is discretionary consumer bought into a tightening cycle, analyst revisions are still deteriorating (strong sell 2 to 3 over four months), and a governance fix takes quarters to show up in comps while the horizon is 15 sessions.
recommendations.counter_argument: THE STRONGEST CASE AGAINST IS THE SHAPE OF THE TRADE, NOT THE STORY. The 127.15 target is 4.47 ATR and +20% away, and from 2026-11-25 the 12-09 print is session 10 of a 15-session horizon, which leaves five sessions afterwards to travel it. So the only realistic path to target inside the horizon is a roughly 4.5-ATR upward gap on 2026-12-10, while the 95.50 stop is 2.23 ATR away and reachable by ordinary drift. The claimed edge is therefore not 'LULU re-rates' — it is 'LULU gaps up ~20% on the print before drifting 10% down', and the win probability was cut from 42% to 38% to say so (+0.14R against a 33.3% break-even, 4.7 points of claimed edge rather than 8.7). 4.47 ATR is inside the repo's own 6.0 swing guide, so the target is not stretched — but it is event-dependent in a way the ratio does not show. SECOND, MY OWN MACRO WORK. This report concludes the Fed is hiking into a weakening consumer and the right posture is defensive, which argues against premium athleisure at all. The answer that survives scrutiny is the de-rating: LULU is 53.1% off its 225.98 52-week high (44.9% off the 200-bar range high the thesis quotes), 16.7% below its SMA200, and the sell side is at 4.8% bullish — 1 strong buy and 1 buy against 31 holds, 6 sells and 3 strong sells. That is the opposite of a crowded consensus long, and it is the specific reason DG and KR were rejected this morning while this was kept: they sit within 4% of their highs with no room for an honest stop, and this does not. THIRD, THE TARGETS LANDED TOO NEATLY. All three of today's ideas computed to exactly 2.0000x risk to the penny, which is the signature CLAUDE.md warns about. Checked rather than assumed: LULU's target at the true SMA200 of 127.31 gives 2.015:1, GIII's at the 37.5387 range high gives 2.17:1, DKS's at a 14.8x multiple (175.82) gives 2.02:1 — so each was rounded DOWN to the floor from a real level that cleared it anyway. The exactness is a tell that the numbers were tuned to the floor, but no target was stretched to reach it. FOURTH, CONVICTION.
